To knock down or to demolish, usually a building.

examples.english: He overcame, however, the enervating drowsiness that kept destroying him; He walked a lot and in a hurry he had an atrocious desire to see a welcoming gesture. […]
examples.text: Se sobrepuso, no obstante, al enervante sopor que le arroñaba; anduvo mucho y de prisa le habia entrado una gana atroz de ver un gesto acogedor […]
examples.translation: He overcame, however, the enervating drowsiness that kept destroying him; He walked a lot and in a hurry he had an atrocious desire to see a welcoming gesture. […]

examples.english: […] of charity they have to bury him, while in the straw of filthy pallets, jewelry rusts and doubloons are demolished […]
examples.ref: 1954, Francisco Villaespesa, Federico de Mendizábal, Poesías completas, volume 2, page 692:
examples.text: […] de caridad tienen que hacerle el entierro, mientras en la paja de inmundos jergones, se enmohecen joyas y arroñan doblones […]
examples.translation: […] of charity they have to bury him, while in the straw of filthy pallets, jewelry rusts and doubloons are demolished […]

examples.english: This crumbling stone wall, this demolished castle which once defended a bridge which is now submerged, this soil which they worked, or the parade ground full of poppies […]
examples.ref: 1975, Luis Cortés Vázquez, Mi libro de Zamora, page 46:
examples.text: Este cerco amurallado a medio caer, este castillo arroñado que sirvió para defender el puente hoy inexistente y anegado, este campo labrado o el patio de armas lleno de amapolas […]
examples.translation: This crumbling stone wall, this demolished castle which once defended a bridge which is now submerged, this soil which they worked, or the parade ground full of poppies […]

examples.english: As soon as they took two steps down the alley, they tripped over a lump lying on the muddy ground; and a woman who came from the corral, disheveled, wringing her hands, surrounded them.
examples.ref: 1984, Emilia Pardo Bazán (condesa de), Marina Mayoral, Cuentos y novelas de la tierra, volume 1, page 64:
examples.text: Apenas avanzaron dos pasos por la calleja, tropezaron con un bulto que yacía en el fangoso suelo; y una mujer que venía de la corraliza, desmelenada, retorciéndose las manos, los arroñó.
examples.translation: As soon as they took two steps down the alley, they tripped over a lump lying on the muddy ground; and a woman who came from the corral, disheveled, wringing her hands, surrounded them.

examples.english: A beggar, no matter how knocked down and misused he may be, begs, for God and for his nails and his mercy, for a crust of bread.
examples.ref: 1995, Alonso Zamora Vicente, La Otra Esquina de La Lengua, page 109:
examples.text: Un mendigo, por arroñado y en mal uso que esté, suplica, por Dios y por sus clavos y su misericordia, un coscurro de pan.
examples.translation: A beggar, no matter how knocked down and misused he may be, begs, for God and for his nails and his mercy, for a crust of bread.

glosses: To knock down or to demolish, usually a building.
